rounds.text: Adroit Infotech Ltd is trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 27 per share against a current market price of ₹ 11.2, offering a substantial margin of safety of 58.0% [E44, E45]. The stock trades at attractive valuation multiples relative to both its own book value and broader sector benchmarks, featuring a price-to-book ratio of 0.78x on filed statements and 0.82x against a sector benchmark of 2.02x [E2, E7], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 5.86x compared to a sector benchmark of 11.25x [E11]. Fundamental momentum is robust, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 54% [E17], a five-year compounded sales growth of 51% [E15], and a massive 281% surge in trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth [E21]. Furthermore, cash generation is exceptionally strong, backed by a cash conversion ratio of 2.18x and operating cash flow reaching Rs 7.20 Cr in March 2026, which represents 170% of operating profit and fully backs reported earnings with real cash [E34, E35, E37]. Technical momentum also supports the bullish thesis, as the stock sits comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E49, E50]. Conceded: the company carries a low return on equity, registering a median of 4% over the last five years and 1% over the last three years [E27, E28, E62], while reporting a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

Despite top-line expansion, Adroit Infotech Ltd carries severe fundamental weaknesses, starting with persistently low profitability metrics such as a 3-year median return on equity of just 1% [E28] and an overall ROE of 4.25% that lags far behind the sector benchmark of 10.41% [E9]. Operating performance is deteriorating across multiple horizons, highlighted by a sharp ten-percentage-point contraction in TTM operating margins down to 9% compared to 19% three years prior [E30], alongside an inconsistent margin trend [E32, E33] and negative 3-year compounded profit growth of -4% [E20]. Balance sheet risk is escalating concurrently, as borrowings jumped significantly to Rs 26.45 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 16.22 Cr a year earlier [E40], and reported earnings are further compromised by including Rs 4.02 Cr in other income [E63]. Furthermore, insider commitment is slipping with promoter holding down to 42.99% in June 2026 from 45.07% in September 2023 [E42], while historical shareholder wealth creation remains dismal, marked by a 10-year compounded share price decline of -15% [E22], a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -94.5% [E52], and high annualised volatility of 64.2% [E53]. Conceded: [E35] operating cash flow reached Rs 7.20 Cr in March 2026 with strong cash conversion [E34].

Conceded: [E28, E20, E52]. While the bear points to low historical ROE and a past 3-year profit contraction, these lag indicators ignore explosive recent acceleration where trailing twelve-month sales surged 54% [E17] and profit skyrocketed 281% [E21], vastly outperforming the sector median profit growth of 11% [E74]. The concern over margin contraction [E30] is counterbalanced by stellar cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 7.20 Cr in March 2026—representing an elite 2.18x cash conversion rate where profits are fully backed by cash [E34]. The nominal increase in borrowings [E40] is supported by a manageable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.34x [E38] and a solid current ratio of 1.96x [E39], while promoter commitment has actively rebounded with a 4.71% increase in holdings over the most recent quarter [E60]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.78x against a sector benchmark of 2.02x [E7], alongside an attractive EV/EBITDA of 5.86x compared to the 11.25x sector benchmark [E11]. Finally, fears regarding overall mispricing are mitigated by a compelling discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 27 leaving a 58% margin of safety [E44, E45], combined with strong technical momentum as the price sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E49, E50].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E34, E44, E45, E49, E50]. The bull's reliance on recent surging sales and stellar cash conversion ignores the fact that earnings quality is severely compromised by the inclusion of Rs. 4.02 Cr in other income [E63]. Furthermore, while the debt-to-equity ratio is cited as manageable at 0.34x [E38], total borrowings actually expanded sharply to Rs. 26.45 Cr up from Rs. 16.22 Cr a year prior [E40]. The touted low price-to-book and EV/EBITDA ratios [E7, E11] fail to compensate for deeply entrenched structural inefficiencies, highlighted by an abysmal 3-year median ROE of just 1% [E28] and an overall low historical ROE of 1.46% over the last 3 years [E62]. The claim of rebounding promoter commitment [E60] overlooks the broader reality that promoter holding has actually declined over the medium term from 45.07% to 42.99% [E42]. Finally, the bull dismisses historical volatility and drawdowns, yet the asset carries a massive annualized volatility of 64.2% alongside a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -94.5% [E52, E53].
